newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank asks finance firms to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank asks finance firms to cut rates.

text.p: Thai finance firms have been asked by the central bank to start cutting deposit rates from Monday, sources from the Thai Finance Companies Association told Reuters on Monday.
The move was aimed at helping ease the burdens of the cash-strapped finance sector which had competed for public funds by setting high and unrealistic rates, they said.
According to a central bank circular dated June 18 and seen by Reuters, finance companies were advised to limit their call rates to about 15 percent, plus or minus 2.0 percent.
The overnight interbank rate stood at 18 percent on Monday morning.
An executive at one medium-sized finance firm said companies were unlikely to cut deposit rates as instructed until the industry undertook the action collectively.

"The measure is good as it will cool down the competition. But are some finance firms ready as the liquidity problems have gone from bad to worse?" he said. "If a few companies refuse to cooperate, the rest will also follow suit.'
Industry sources say sustained tight liquidity in the past few months has forced some small finance firms to offer promisory notes with annual interest rates of over 20 percent.
The practice caused hefty interest burdens for these financially-troubled companies and increased the chance of maturity mismatching.
